sentences.text:
Rajkumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:50751) on 11
December, 2024

Author: Kuldeep Mathur Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2024:RJ-JD:50751]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 15312/2024 Rajkumar S/o Shri Vedprakash, Aged About 24 Years, R/o 2 M.l Dhani, P.s. Anoopgarh, Dist Anoopgarh. Raj.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(At Present Lodged In Sub Jail Suratgarh)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. S.R. Godara For Respondent(s) : Mr. Shrawan Singh Rathore, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 11/12/2024

This application for bail under Section 483 BNSS has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.420/2024 registered at Police Station Suratgarh, Dist. Sri Ganganagar, for the offences under Sections 376, 384, 342, 323, 506, 379,
420,382,120-B of IPC.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner who is aged about 24 years has been falsely implicated in a criminal case.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the statements of the prosecutrix 'M' recorded under Section 183 BNSS and various documents attached with the bail application, learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix who is a mature girl voluntarily eloped with the present petitioner in the month of [2024:RJ-JD:50751] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-15312/2024]
February, 2024 and solemnized marriage with him as per the Hindu Vedic Rights and Customs.
The marriage solemnized between them was also got registered as per the provisions of Uttar Pradesh Marriage Registration Rules, 2017 by the Marriage Registration Officer at Gaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

Attention of the Court was also drawn towards the application jointly submitted by the petitioner Rajkumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:50751) on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173485413/
1 and the prosecutrix before the Court of Addl. District Judge No.1, Anoopgarh under Section 13(B)
Hindu Marriage Act seeking mutual divorce.

entities.text: Court of Addl. District Judge No.1, Anoopgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel submitted that on relations turning sour between the petitioner and the prosecutrix, the prosecutrix has lodged a false FIR against the petitioner alleging inter alia that the petitioner established physical relationship with her on a false pretext of marriage and thereafter,
committed forcible sexual assault/rape upon her on multiple occasions by threatening her to circulate her videos and photographs on the social media platforms.

It was submitted that sufficient material is available on record to establish that the prosecutrix was having a love affair with the present petitioner and she voluntarily ran away from her parental house and stayed with the petitioner for more than 3-4 months at various places such as Bikaner,
Anoopgarh, Gaziabad, etc.
However, despite having ample opportunities, she did not disclosed the factum of she being subjected to forcible sexual assault/rape by the present petitioner to anyone.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody; investigation against him has already been [2024:RJ-JD:50751] (3 of 4) [CRLMB-15312/2024] concluded and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail may be granted to the accused- petitioner.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor has vehemently opposed the bail application.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case and having perused the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 183 BNSS and the documents/material placed on record by the counsel for the petitioner, this Court prima facie finds that the argument of learned counsel for the petitioner that the prosecutrix was having a mutual relationship with the petitioner and she voluntarily eloped with the present petitioner and remained in his company for more than 3-4 months, cannot be brushed aside at this stage.

On a careful perusal of the case file,
this Court also finds that the investigation against the petitioner has already been completed and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of petitioner influencing the remaining material prosecution witnesses of the case or fleeing away from justice or tampering with the evidence, in case he is enlarged on bail.

Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case,
this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 BNSS is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Rajkumar S/o Shri Vedprakash arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.420/2024 registered at Police Station Suratgarh, Dist. Sri Ganganagar, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he [2024:RJ-JD:50751] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-15312/2024] furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.
